front.title: Options representation in SCHC YANG Data Models

abstract.t: Keeping option identifiers in SCHC Rules simplifies interoperability and the evolution of SCHC compression when a protocol introduces options that the current SCHC implementation does not know. This document explains why the Field Identifiers (FIDs) defined for CoAP options in RFC 9363 do not scale: a FID must be allocated, standardized and implemented for each option a protocol defines, before any Rule can describe that option. It presents an evolution of the compression Rule defined in RFC 9363, in which an entry refers to an option by the pair (option space, option number), called a Universal Option, and in which entries are indexed, ordered and can reference one another. It also presents a data model dedicated to CoAP, which processes options directly from the option number carried in the message, instead of mapping each option to a FID of its own.
